label: H.R. 9010

latest_action.text: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 580.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 9010 sets forth the federal appropriations and related policy requirements for the legislative branch of the U.S. government for fiscal year 2027. It allocates specific funding amounts for the House of Representatives, joint congressional committees, the Capitol Police, the Library of Congress, the Government Publishing Office, the Government Accountability Office, and other legislative support agencies. The bill also includes restrictions on technology procurement, guidelines for workplace training, and administrative rules for managing leftover funds.

affected_groups.effect: Receive salaries, representational allowances, and office funding, while facing restrictions on vehicle leases, bans on member cost-of-living pay adjustments, and mandatory in-person conduct training if under active ethics review.
affected_groups.group: Members of Congress and House Employees

affected_groups.effect: Receive salary and operational expense funding, including specialized security allowances and basic training costs covered via the Department of Homeland Security.
Receive specific operating appropriations for fiscal year 2027 to carry out research, auditing, publishing, and library services.
affected_groups.group: Legislative Support Agencies (CRS, CBO, GAO, GPO, Library of Congress)

key_provisions: Provides FY2027 funding for House of Representatives operations, including leadership offices, member representational allowances ($900,000,000), intern compensation allowances, and committee staff and expenses.
Appropriates funds for the Capitol Police, including salaries, general expenses, and basic training covered by the Department of Homeland Security.

Prohibits the use of funds to procure certain information technology equipment or drones manufactured by entities tied to specific foreign adversaries or listed on designated defense, commerce, and homeland security lists.
Requires that unused amounts remaining in members' representational allowances be deposited into the Treasury for federal deficit reduction or debt reduction.
Mandates in-person workplace rights and responsibilities training for any Member of Congress who has a publicly disclosed matter under active review by the House Ethics Committee.

Blocks funds from being used to maintain or establish computer networks unless those networks block the viewing, downloading, and exchanging of pornography, with exceptions for law enforcement and official investigations.
Prohibits cost-of-living adjustments for Members of Congress during fiscal year 2027.
missing_information: Senate funding levels and provisions are omitted because of the longstanding practice of each chamber determining its own requirements.
Total aggregate spending figures for the entire bill are not explicitly summarized in a single aggregate total in the provided text.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 9010 sets forth the federal appropriations and related policy requirements for the legislative branch of the U.S. government for fiscal year 2027. It allocates specific funding amounts for the House of Representatives, joint congressional committees, the Capitol Police, the Library of Congress, the Government Publishing Office, the Government Accountability Office, and other legislative support agencies. The bill also includes restrictions on technology procurement, guidelines for workplace training, and administrative rules for managing leftover funds.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents the primary funding mechanism for the entire legislative branch of the federal government for fiscal year 2027. It determines operational budgets, staffing levels, security provisions, and administrative rules for congressional offices and support agencies, carrying a sweeping impact across the internal operations of Congress and its supporting entities.
